name: Clay World
summary: Stop-motion plasticine miniature set: soft gradient-built clay figures with fingerprints, warm studio light and 12 fps boil.
description: Everything looks hand-rolled from modelling clay and shot on a tabletop miniature set: characters are stacks of soft lumpy balls and sausages without any outlines, each lit by a warm top-left key light with inner ambient occlusion, a warm rim along the top edge, faint thumbprints and a broad soft specular. The ground is a set of flat clay sheets (meadow, soil, purple clay, ochre paths, sunken glossy ponds) with raised, bevelled edges and a lumpy hand-pressed surface. Animation steps at 12 fps and every frame is a slightly different 'boil' of the same model, which sells the stop-motion feel.
avoidFor: grim or horror games that need hard darkness
projects with hundreds of distinct character designs

difficulty.why: Soft gradient shapes are forgiving, but every new asset has to be assembled from lumpy primitives painted back to front through the full clay() painter (key light, fingerprints, inner AO, rim, soft spec) and baked once per frame with its own seed; getting a new figure to really read as plasticine usually takes a few iteration passes.

technique.resolution: Native resolution; sprites are baked once at K = clamp(round(screen px per world unit × 1.2), 3, 5) px per world unit; ground is baked in 256-unit chunks at up to 2.5 px per unit.
technique.summary: Every body part goes through one 'clay()' painter: flat fill, radial key-light gradient, a tiled fingerprint pattern, inner ambient occlusion and a warm rim light produced by blurred offset shadows of the shape's outside, then a broad tilted soft specular. Parts are stacked back-to-front and cast soft contact shadows onto parts already painted.
technique.linework: No outlines at all. The only 'lines' are pressed grooves: a dark furrow rgba(58,22,18,a) of width w (0.3–1.1 units, round caps) with a lighter lip rgba(255,240,220,0.75a) of width 0.5w drawn 0.55w lower.
technique.shading: Soft volumetric gradients per part: radial gradient from lighten(col,0.2) at the upper-left (-0.25rx, -0.5ry) through the base colour (stop 0.5) to darken(col,0.4) at radius 1.22R; inner AO with alpha 0.5 along the bottom, warm rim alpha 0.42 along the top.
technique.lighting: One warm studio key light from the top-left (ground light vector (-0.42, -0.907)); shadows drift to plum (#401a34) not black, highlights to warm white (#fffbf0). Carved faces and cores glow candle-yellow (#fff7c4 → #ffd458 → #ff8f22) with additive halos. A warm brown vignette frames the screen.
technique.texture: Tileable 192 px fingerprint tile (concentric thumbprint arcs + tool smears, dark line plus light line 0.9 px lower, alpha 0.07–0.1) on every part; ground uses a tileable lumpy height field (2 texels per unit) whose diagonal derivative lights the surface ±10–15%.

paletteRules: Saturated but slightly muted 'toy clay' colours; nothing neon, nothing pure black or pure white.
Shadows are always mixed toward plum (#401a34 / rgba(58,20,40)) and highlights toward warm white (#fffbf0); never shade with grey.
Ground sheets are mid-value (luminance ~35–65%) so the brighter, glossier characters pop in front of them.
Each creature family has a two-tone scheme (e.g. purple top layer over cream body) so groups read as clusters of colour.
Glowing elements use only the candle ramp #fff7c4 → #ffd458 → #ff8f22, added with 'lighter' compositing.
Roughly 60% ground greens/purples, 25% character colours, 15% warm accents (orange, gold, cream UI).

typography.role: Titles, HUD numbers, card names, floating numbers (rendered as extruded clay letters)

typography.role: Body text, labels, card descriptions, hints

world.summary: A tabletop set of flat clay sheets composed like a model railway table: a calm green meadow sheet, one winding ochre path rolled to a constant width, small furrowed garden beds, dusty-purple heath patches and sunken glossy ponds. Per-pixel signed distance gives each raised sheet a lit bevel, a rolled lip and a soft cast shadow (ponds are pressed in), a tileable lumpy height texture gives the hand-pressed surface, and decals gather in drifts, fringes and posies instead of an even sprinkle.
layers: Meadow sheet #76a454 <-> #8cac5a blended by low-frequency noise, lumpy height texture at full strength
Garden beds (soil #986c4a, fbm/460 - 0.64) with modelling-tool furrow rows 7 units apart pressed across them
Sunken ponds #7ebad2 (fbm/420 - 0.675): darker wet bank, inverted bevel, smooth glossy surface, studio-light reflections
The path #d6a262: half-width 13 minus |n|/|grad n| of a warped 1/1500 perlin -> constant ~26-unit width; raised bevel and cast shadow

Decals: grass imprints and rolled sprouts only in drifts (smoothstep(0.56, 0.78, noise/170)); sprouts and pebbles fringing every sheet edge; flower posies of 4-7 where a sparse patch field peaks; lily-pad rafts; thumbprints and footprints on the path; worms and pebbles in the beds

characters.summary: Characters are assemblies of 10–25 clay primitives (ellipses, capsules, lumpy Catmull-Rom blobs, custom silhouettes) painted back to front with the clay() painter, each with its own contact shadow on the parts behind. Proportions are chunky toy proportions: big head (~60% of the height), tiny stubby limbs, googly eyes. The main character (a round orange gourd head with a carved glowing face, blue overalls, green scarf) is ~21 units wide and ~33 tall; creatures are two-tone root bulbs with googly eyes (~21 × 22), a glossy white floating sheet (~20 × 24) and a large lumpy mauve root giant with glowing cracks (~37 × 64). Each animation frame is baked separately with a different random seed so lumps and fingerprints shift (boil).
rules: No outlines: silhouettes separate through value contrast, AO at the bottom of every part and the soft ground shadow.
Heads and key shapes get a strong glossy highlight (spec 0.55, gloss 0.7); limbs a weak one (spec 0.15–0.35).
Faces are either carved holes with candle glow, white clay eyeballs with glossy black pupils, or dark sockets pressed into the clay.
Details such as head ribs, cloth folds and wood grain are pressed grooves, never drawn lines.
Creatures are lighter/glossier than the ground and always carry eyes; small creatures sit at ~0.6× the main character's height, large ones ~2×.

The main character walks through 8 drawn poses + 1 stand pose at 12 fps (contact, down, passing, up twice), arms and head one drawing behind; small creatures hop in 8 steps on twos; whole sprites also squash/stretch 3-10% per step.
Mirror sprites for facing; the light still comes from the top-left in both directions because the mirror is baked from the same lit art (accepted cheat).

props.summary: Props are built with the same clay() painter and back-to-front assembly as the characters: lumpy foliage balls, capsule trunks and posts, pressed grooves for grain and cracks, glossy berries. Each prop has a fixed soft plum-brown shadow ellipse.
rules: Trees: capsule trunk r 3.4 (#865e40) with 3 grooves, 5 lumpy foliage balls r 8–11 alternating ±5% lightness, glossy red berries or white blossoms; shadow 17 × 5.5.
Bushes: 4 lumps + berries; shadow 14 × 4.5. Mushrooms: dome + cream spots.
Fences: capsule posts and rails with pressed grooves.
Gourds with pressed ribs; gravestones as grey slabs (#9a96a4) with a pressed cross and a chipped-corner groove.
Hay domes from 90 straw strokes; rocks as 1–2 grey lumps.
2–4 baked variants per prop; light from the top-left like everything else.

Placement is composed: a woodland field makes groves (trees inside with mushrooms underneath, bushes on the rim); cattails ring pond shores; fences and rocks follow the path edges; pumpkin patches and hay fill the garden beds; gravestones stand in little groups on the heath; the open meadow stays nearly empty.
Trees, bushes and cattails sway in a breeze sampled at 12 fps (on twos), each on its own phase, skewed around the base.

effects.name: Clay crumbs
effects.how: Impacts and disappearing figures throw off 3–18 small baked clay balls (2 × 1.85 units, in the figure colours) that fly with gravity 300 and squash to 1.25 × 0.72 when they touch the ground.

effects.name: Splat
effects.how: A vanished figure leaves a flat lumpy clay pancake (4.6 × 2.4 units plus 3 droplets) that pops in with outBack over 8% of its 1.7–2.2 s life and fades/flattens in the last 30%.

effects.name: Squash-out
effects.how: Disappearing figures scale x by 1 + 0.7k and y by 1 - 0.8k (k = outQuad over 0.55 of the time) with a fading white-cream flash overlay (#fff8ec).

effects.name: Impact flash
effects.how: A cream-tinted copy of the sprite is drawn at alpha min(0.55, flash × 0.8) while the sprite squashes 16% wide / 15% flat, plus an additive soft white flash puff (6–9 units, 0.12 s).

effects.name: Candle glow
effects.how: Carved faces, lantern collectibles and glowing creature cores get an additive radial glow sprite (rgba(255,214,120,0.85) → rgba(255,140,40,0)) pulsing ±0.08–0.1 alpha on the 12 fps step.

effects.name: Seed projectile
effects.how: A baked glossy cream seed (#f8e8be) with a soft tapered streak behind it (rgba(255,244,214,0.75) → 0 over 11.5 units); the seed flips in steps by scaling y with 0.6 + 0.4|cos|.

effects.name: Rise from the ground
effects.how: Appearing figures emerge from a dark clay mound and are revealed row by row in 8 discrete steps (only the part above the feet line is drawn) with a 12% wobble.

effects.name: Dust puffs
effects.how: Dash and landing dust are soft beige radial blobs (rgba(236,214,182,0.9)) that grow 0.6 → 1.5× and fade over 0.25–0.6 s.

atmosphere.summary: A warm tabletop studio: one key light from the top-left on every sprite, bevel and UI gradient, soft plum-brown shadows instead of black, additive candle glows for practical lights, and a warm brown vignette with a soft top light band over the whole screen.
rules: Key light top-left everywhere: sprite gradients, highlights, ground bevels (L = (-0.42, -0.907)), pebbles, UI radial gradients at 30% 18%.

Figure shadows: a radial sprite rgba(44,24,16,0.5) → 0.34 @ 0.45 → 0 stretched to an ellipse (main character 10.2 × 3.6, small creature 8.8 × 3.0, large creature 21 × 6.6, floating 6.2 × 2.3 at alpha 0.6), shifted +8% of rx to the right.
Shadow tints drift to plum (#401a34, AO rgba(58,20,40), contact rgba(52,22,24)); highlights to warm white (#fffbf0); never grey or black.

Practical lights: additive glow rgba(255,214,120,0.85) → rgba(255,170,70,0.35) @ 0.35 → 0 for the light pool under the main character (34 × 18, alpha 0.16), the carved face (11 × 10, alpha 0.3 ± 0.08), lanterns (12, alpha 0.45 ± 0.1), creature cores (11, alpha 0.32 ± 0.1) and collectibles.

Screen overlay (one 320 × 180 sprite stretched): elliptical vignette (scaled 1 × 0.62) rgba(70,34,16,0) at r 70 → 0.12 at 60% → rgba(56,26,12,0.46) at r 215; warm top band rgba(255,232,206,0.24) → 0 over the top 19%; faint bottom band rgba(255,226,196,0.2); whole-screen warm wash rgba(255,186,110,0.04).
Menu backdrops: radial-gradient(rgba(255,206,140,.28), rgba(46,22,10,.7) 78%) with backdrop-filter: blur(3px) saturate(.75); a desaturated variant adds grayscale(.7) brightness(.7).

ui.summary: HUD elements are soft clay slabs: cream radial-gradient panels with inner top highlight, inner bottom shadow, a solid 5 px darker 'thickness' below and a soft drop shadow; irregular border radii so no panel is perfectly round; bars are pressed brown grooves with glossy pill fills; numbers are Chewy with stacked extruded text-shadows; a faint thumbprint (repeating radial gradient) sits in a panel corner.

motion: Everything steps at 12 fps (on twos) and boils: per step, a hash nudges scale (±2-3.5%) and rotation (±0.025-0.04 rad), and every baked frame has its own lump seed.

Main character: 8 drawn walk poses (contact, down, passing, up x2) at 12 fps from a pose table; arms one drawing behind the legs, the heavy head one drawing behind the body; down poses squash 1.045 x 0.955 at draw time.
Small creatures hop in 8 steps (crouch, take-off stretch, rise, apex, fall, fall stretch, landing squash, settle) with 4 boiled drawings held on twos; every creature on its own phase.
Floating creature: two-partial hover on twos, stretching 4.5% while it rises; large creature: 4-frame stomp with an 8% contact squash.
Hit: a thumb-press dent that springs back (e^(-9t)cos(26t), stepped at 24 fps), a 0.28 rad tilt away from the blow and the pale flash copy.

Removal: anticipation stretch, pressed flat by an invisible thumb with a twist, the clay disc shivers and sinks into the set (40 steps); ghosts slump and melt into a puddle; crumbs 0.8 s, splat decal ~2 s.
Spawn: a clay mound swells, the creature rises out of the ground row by row with a wobble, the mound shrinks away.
Props sway in a stepped breeze; collectibles bob and pop with outBack; numbers pop 0.4 -> 1.25 -> 1.
do: Build every shape from the clay() painter: base, radial key light, fingerprints, inner AO, rim, soft spec.
Paint parts back to front so each part casts a soft contact shadow (offset ~0.45, 1.4 units) onto what is behind it.
Press details in as grooves (dark furrow + light lip below) instead of drawing lines.
Quantise all animation to 12 fps and re-bake each frame with a new seed for boil.
Keep the light from the top-left everywhere: sprites, ground bevels, pebbles, UI gradients.
Give every figure a soft plum-brown ground shadow (rgba(44,24,16,0.5) centre).
Use the candle glow ramp for anything magical or important so it reads instantly.
dont: Don't draw dark outlines or ink lines; it instantly turns the look into cartoon vector art.
Don't use hard cel-shading bands or pure black shadows; clay shading is always soft and plum-tinted.
Don't animate smoothly at 60 fps; tweened motion destroys the stop-motion feel.
Don't use perfect geometric circles for organic parts; use lumpy blobs (11 points, ±6–20% radius noise).
Don't add high-contrast noise or grain on top; texture must be subtle fingerprints and lumps.
Don't make highlights tiny and sharp (that reads as hard plastic or candy); clay specular is broad and soft, only heads get a small glossy dot.
Don't use neon or fully saturated colours; plasticine pigment is slightly chalky.
performance: All characters, props, collectibles and particles are baked once into canvases at 3–5 px per world unit (the clay() painter with shadowBlur is far too expensive per frame); per frame only drawImage blits, a few additive glow sprites and the screen overlay remain. The ground is the hot spot: per-pixel SDF bevel plus height-texture lookup per 256-unit chunk, computed incrementally with a generator and cached. Fingerprint tile (192 px) and height texture (256×256) are built once at init. Composition adds work only at chunk build time (furrow rows, the path gradient, drift fields), which is spread over frames by the chunk generator; per frame the props add a stepped skew transform and the walk adds no cost (8 baked poses instead of 4).
